_comment: Two projects, three crate sets, two acquisition paths.
ruff publishes ONE release across TWO version lines: `ruff`, `ruff_linter` and `ruff_wasm`
track the product line (0.16.7) while the 28 library crates sit on a 0.0.x line (0.0.13).
Verified 2026-09-15: ruff_linter 0.16.7 declares `ruff_python_ast ^0.0.13` and 17 further
ruff_* dependencies at ^0.0.13, and every crate in both lines was published 2026-09-10. They
are one release. `crate_sets` carries one version each because build.crate_specs assigns
spec['version'] from the set, so splitting them is what keeps the index from claiming a
version that does not exist on crates.io.
pyrefly publishes nothing usable: crates.io `pyrefly` is a name squat at 0.0.1 (2025-03-13,
'Coming soon to crates.io.') and every pyrefly_* crate is absent. docs.rs therefore has
nothing to serve, so acquire.py produces the rustdoc JSON locally from the pinned tag and
build.py reads it offline. DESIGN.md B13 authorises exactly this fallback.
Executing either binary during acquisition is governed by ADR-0046.

repository.name: pyrefly-ruff
repository.title: The ruff crate family and pyrefly
repository.description: Pinned API surface, tool catalogs and documentation for ruff 0.16.7 / 0.0.13 and pyrefly 1.3.1 — the two Rust Python-analysis toolchains.

_comment: The versions the tool-catalog capture installs into the capsule and asserts before
recording anything. These MUST match the crate-set pins: this workstation has ruff 0.14.4
on PATH (pinned by the host repository) and a 0.51.1 checker, so a capture from PATH would
describe different software than the rustdoc index describes. Measured 2026-09-15: the
0.14.4 binary reports 934 rules while ruff_linter 0.16.7 carries 970 Rule variants, which
is exactly the discrepancy the assertion exists to prevent.
`checker` is the role name used by oracles.py; `checker_package` is what uv installs.

crate_sets.name: ruff-product
crate_sets.note: The product version line. ruff_linter holds all 934 lint rules; `ruff` is the CLI crate and `ruff_wasm` the browser binding.

crate_sets.name: ruff-lib
crate_sets.note: The embeddable library line. These are the crates a downstream Rust consumer depends on, and the crates pyrefly itself builds upon.

crate_sets.name: pyrefly
crate_sets.note: document_private_items is load-bearing: the clap Args structs that define the CLI are private, and without them the command surface is absent from the index while the build still succeeds.

git.lock_note: The repository commits its own Cargo.lock, so resolution is pinned upstream. It also carries [patch.crates-io] backtrace = { git = 'https://github.com/rust-lang/backtrace-rs', rev = 'df979dcf80027eb047d7bb9e0874710c15009f31' }, which acquisition must resolve and record.
git.toolchain_note: The checkout's own rust-toolchain.toml pins channel = 'stable', which cannot emit rustdoc JSON, so cargo_env overrides RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN with a dated producer identity from config/toolchains.toml. NOT the current nightly-2026-09-13: measured 2026-09-15, `allocative` 0.3.6 fails to compile on it with E0119. Its build.rs sets cfg(rust_nightly) by string-matching `rustc --version`, then enables feature(never_type) and adds `impl Allocative for !`, which conflicts with its own `impl Allocative for Infallible` once the two unify. The break landed between 2026-08-18 and 2026-09-13; nightly-2026-08-18 compiles it and still emits format_version 61, the same version docs.rs serves for the ruff crates, so both crate sets are read by one parser adapter.

excluded_members.pyrefly_bench_harness: a benchmark harness, not part of the analysis API
excluded_members.pyrefly_lsp_test: a test helper for the LSP suite
excluded_members.pyrefly_wasm: version 0.0.0, not 1.3.1, and a cdylib for wasm32 — indexing it under this crate set's version would assert a version it does not carry

corpora.name: ruff-docs
corpora.note: Recent ruff tags carry no `v` prefix; older ones (v0.4.10) do. The per-rule documentation is NOT here — it comes from `ruff rule --all --output-format json`, which is richer and machine-readable. These are the non-rule pages: configuration, linter, formatter, editors, faq, versioning, preview.

corpora.name: pyrefly-docs
corpora.note: 35 pages. configuration.mdx is 80 KB and error-kinds.mdx 73 KB — the two largest, and the narrative layer rustdoc cannot supply. import-resolution.mdx answers the question this skill exists for.

corpora.name: pyrefly-conformance
corpora.note: The Python typing conformance suite and the checker's measured results against it. `conformance.result` is the load-bearing file: a JSON map of test file to the deviations found, where an empty list means fully conformant. That is machine-checkable evidence of which typing features are supported, rather than a claim. `conformance.exp` is deliberately excluded -- it is 470 KB of raw expected-error dumps that `.result` already summarises.
